confirmed: URL scheme. Coverage (BTC verified). The S3 ListObjects v1 listing for data/spot/monthly/klines/BTCUSDT/1m/ has 220 objects (110 zips and 110 CHECKSUMs), contiguous 2017-08..2026-09, with MaxKeys 1000 and IsTruncated=false. Listing pitfalls. <ChecksumAlgorithm>CRC64NVME</ChecksumAlgorithm><ChecksumType>FULL_OBJECT</ChecksumType> sits between ETag and Size on exactly the 40 objects for months 2025-02..2026-09. The earliest is the 2025-02 zip, uploaded 2025-03-04; the 2025-01 zip, uploaded 2025-02-08, has none. A regex that expects ETag to be followed directly by Size matched only 180 of 220 objects. The site uses BUCKET_URL='https://s3-ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com/data.binance.vision' (index.html:44) and list.js createS3QueryUrl/marker (list.js:195-232).

Publication lag (BTC). Every monthly zip since 2025-05 has a LastModified on the first Monday of the next month, 07:12-11:13 UTC, a lag of 0.30-6.46 days. The irregular months match: 2024-09 at 14.52 days, 2023-01 at 17.03 days, 2023-08 at 18.06 days. Months 2020-01..2021-05 all show 2021-06-22, and 2022-03 shows 2022-09-02. README.md:5 quote verified. ETag equals MD5. This holds for the researcher's three files (re-checked with a fresh HEAD: d5b0e8e4..., 8e9ca636..., 34fb47fd...) and for my own download of BTCUSDT-1m-2025-01.zip (1db0d334b7602fd2f2300c4a75467edf). The BTC listing has no multipart ETags. Objects are SSE-S3 (x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256).

CHECKSUM format. The daily file is 91 B, '<64 lowercase hex><2 spaces><basename>', with no trailing newline. The proposed regex matches it, the sha256 matches the zip, and sha256sum -c reports OK. The README documents this check (README.md:88-97). The monthly 88 B size equals 64+2+22, so there is no newline there either.

ZIP structure. Four files were checked, including my 2025-era monthly: each has one entry, method 8, flags 0x0, version needed 2.0, made by Unix 2.0, extra field 0, no comment and no ZIP64 locator. Data starts at offset 52 (monthly) or 55 (daily). The size identities hold exactly, e.g. 52+2,222,688+68+22 = 2,222,830 and 55+65,119+71+22 = 65,267. The largest sampled CSVs are 6,045,956 B (ETH 2020-06) and 7,064,510 B (BTC 2025-01).

zlib-only extractor outline (copied verbatim and run). Its output sha256 equals Python zipfile's (run with -I) for all 4 files. It also extracts a bit-3 data-descriptor variant correctly. It rejects 1-byte and half truncation, an empty buffer, an HTML page, an S3 XML error body, flipped deflate bytes (Z_DATA_ERROR, CRC or ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE), CD size ±1, a flipped CD CRC, EOCD entries=2 and a shifted CD offset: 17/17 as expected. The research's own test-pipeline.mjs reproduces 20/20. zlib.crc32 exists from Node v20.15 / v22.2 (tested on Node v25.2.1).

CSV columns. No header, 12 columns, LF line endings, trailing newline, 8 printed decimals with at most 2 significant, and column 11 always '0' in all 4 files (131,710 rows in total). This matches README.md:20-25 ('obtained from /api/v3/klines').

Microseconds from 2025, CONFIRMED on a monthly file (the researcher had not sampled one). refuted.claim: "There is NO Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, so a browser cannot fetch these files cross-origin" (urlScheme). Repeated as "Fetching directly in the browser does not avoid this. There are no CORS headers" (terms) and "No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, so browser-direct fetching is impossible" (testsDone).
refuted.evidence:
The bucket allows cross-origin GET from any origin on its regional path-style endpoint.
- GET https://s3-ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com/data.binance.vision/data/spot/monthly/klines/BTCUSDT/1m/BTCUSDT-1m-2025-01.zip with 'Origin: https://example.com' returned 200 with 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *', 'Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET' and 'Vary: Origin'. Saved headers: C:\Users\kadir\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-kadir-OneDrive-Masa-st--Wawe-Journal-astro\97ee93d7-3b56-4094-909f-8a419fcb57d4\scratchpad\agents3\binance-review\data\btc_2025_01.headers.
- The listing GET returned the same headers (listing_btc_monthly.headers in that folder).
- An OPTIONS preflight on the object returned 200 with ACAO: *.
- HEAD with an Origin header returns no ACAO, because the CORS rule allows only GET. The research's HEAD-based test was therefore a false negative.
- Only the CloudFront host data.binance.vision shows no CORS: no ACAO on HEAD, and OPTIONS returns 403 from CloudFront. I did not test GET with Origin on CloudFront because of the download cap.
- The site's own index.html:44 fetches the bucket cross-origin from https://data.binance.vision.

The legal conclusion (§4.4) is unaffected, but the technical premise is false.

issues.issue: The CORS / browser-direct claim is false. The S3 regional path-style endpoint returns 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' for GET from any origin. The research tested with HEAD, which the bucket's CORS rule does not include, and so reported 'impossible'.
issues.fix: Restate as follows. data.binance.vision (CloudFront) sends no CORS headers. https://s3-ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com/data.binance.vision/... allows cross-origin GET from any origin, so in-browser fetch plus DecompressionStream('deflate-raw') unzip is technically possible. It is still barred by §4.3/§4.4, and whether that endpoint is approved is unanswered (#511). Test CORS with GET, or with an OPTIONS preflight that has Access-Control-Request-Method: GET, never with HEAD.

issues.issue: The ongoing-traffic figure ('about 4 GETs a day') contradicts the design ('the current month is rebuilt from daily files ... marked partial'). If the run is stateless, it re-downloads every daily of the month on each run: 2 symbols x 2 files x day-of-month, up to about 124 GETs on day 31. That also conflicts with the owner's 'only download what is missing'.
issues.fix: Specify an incremental merge. Download only the new daily (zip and CHECKSUM), read the existing partial candles/{SYM}/{YYYY-MM}.json.gz back from Storage (or a local cache of verified dailies), merge and dedupe, and re-upload. Replace the whole month with the monthly zip once a GET for it returns 200.

issues.issue: The CHECKSUM regex /^([0-9a-f]{64}) {2}(\S+)\s*$/ rejects the equally valid sha256sum binary-mode line '<hex> *<name>'. Only a daily CHECKSUM was ever sampled; the 88 B monthly size fits both separators.
issues.fix: Accept /^([0-9a-fA-F]{64}) [ *](\S+)\s*$/, lowercase the hash before comparing, and keep the basename equality check. Optionally fetch one monthly CHECKSUM during implementation to confirm.

issues.issue: 'Schedule the daily run after about 03:00 UTC' relies on the 2026 lag of 1.4-2.8 h. In 2024 the daily files landed later: 2024-10-27 at 04:58, 2024-10-28 at 05:37 and 2024-12-31 at 03:47 UTC the next day (HEAD Last-Modified).
issues.fix: Make correctness independent of the schedule. Treat a 404 as 'not yet', retry with backoff or on the next run, and record the last successfully imported day in the manifest.

issues.issue: The aggregator rule 'bucket by floor(t/tf)*tf' makes 1w candles start on Thursday 00:00 UTC, because the Unix epoch was a Thursday. Binance and most charting tools start weeks on Monday. Calendar months cannot be bucketed with a fixed tf at all.
issues.fix: For 1w use floor((t-345600)/604800)*604800+345600, which is Monday-aligned. Use calendar arithmetic for 1M. The floor rule stays correct for 1m-1d.

issues.issue: Issue #400 is presented as a reported spot archive gap for 2024-10-28. Its body is only a screenshot. The only text is a third-party comment that also mentions 'Open interest, Long/short ratio', which are futures-only metrics, so the report probably concerns futures data. The spot daily zip size (70,217 B) is normal.
issues.fix: Reword it as 'unconfirmed, likely futures'. Let the importer's gap report settle it when that day is imported.

issues.issue: The zip-bomb guard sets maxOutputLength to the declared size, which comes from the same untrusted file. A forged entry could declare about 4 GiB. Risk is low because the sha256 check runs first, but the guard itself is not a hard limit.
issues.fix: Add an absolute cap (e.g. 64 MiB) before inflating; real monthly 1m CSVs are about 6-8 MB. Keep the sha256-before-extract order.

issues.issue: The terms provenance is incomplete. TERMS_AND_CONDITIONS.md was edited again on 2026-10-16 (d3357a5, 'Update Terms and condition syntax': spacing, case and line breaks only), and the PDF's Last-Modified is 2026-10-16 13:39 GMT. The cited line numbers match the edited version.
issues.fix: Note the 2026-10-16 syntax-only revision; the substance and v1.0 are unchanged. Re-check the terms before any import, because §1.4 allows unilateral amendments.

issues.issue: Two citations are defective: the 2021-09-29 URL resolves to the announcements index, and the 2020-06-28 'start 02:00' comes from the data, not from the cited 'complete' notice.
issues.fix: Drop or replace the 2021-09-29 URL. Say the 2020-06-28 start time is inferred from the archive gap, or cite the original upgrade notice.

corrections:
1) CORS. data.binance.vision (CloudFront) sends no CORS headers. The regional S3 path-style endpoint https://s3-ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com/data.binance.vision/<key> answers a GET from any origin with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (methods: GET). So a browser can fetch the archive directly. The legal analysis still forbids using that in Wawe Journal (§4.3/§4.4), and whether that endpoint is approved is unanswered (#511).
2) CHECKSUM parsing. Accept both the '  ' and ' *' separators.
3) Memory. A 31-day µs-era BTC month is about 7.1 MB of CSV and about 2.2 MB of compact JSON (49 B/candle). Measured gzip -9 output is 623,283 B (13.96 B/candle). The overall 65-103 MB Storage projection stands.
4) Incremental updates. Daily upkeep stays at about 4 GETs only if the new daily is merged into the existing partial month object. A full rebuild grows to about 124 GETs by month end.
5) Citations. The 2020-06-28 'Upgrade Complete' notice gives only the 05:30 UTC resumption; the 02:00 start comes from the data. The 2021-09-29 URL is broken. Issue #400 likely concerns futures.
6) Weekly buckets. Make 1w aggregation Monday-aligned (offset 345,600 s).
7) Terms provenance. Commit bd110bb (2026-09-30) was followed by d3357a5 (2026-10-16, syntax only); the PDF was updated the same day; v1.0 text is unchanged in substance. §6.1 ('exclusively for computational, educational, and research purposes') also supports the blocker.
8) Unverified items, not refuted. I did not check these because of the download cap: the ETHUSDT subtotal of 165,371,486 B, list-type=2 support, and pagination of the full daily prefix. The NextMarker 2018-12-29 is arithmetically consistent: 500 days from 2017-08-17. Also unverified: 'halts hit every symbol at once', for which only an ETH sample exists.
report:
The Binance research holds up. I could refute almost nothing of substance. It has one real technical error, a few citation and estimate slips, and some robustness gaps. The legal blocker is accurately sourced.

What I did:
- Downloads from the Binance bucket: exactly 2, saved to C:\Users\kadir\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-kadir-OneDrive-Masa-st--Wawe-Journal-astro\97ee93d7-3b56-4094-909f-8a419fcb57d4\scratchpad\agents3\binance-review\data\
  - the BTCUSDT monthly 1m S3 listing (listing_btc_monthly.xml, 60,804 B);
  - BTCUSDT-1m-2025-01.zip (2,222,830 B). I chose it because the research never sampled a 2025-era monthly file. Its MD5 equals the ETag.
- Metadata only (no bodies):
  - about 27 HEAD/OPTIONS requests;
  - 3 small site pages from data.binance.vision (index.html, list.js, terms-of-use.html);
  - GitHub raw files and API JSON (README, TERMS, spot CHANGELOG, commits, issues), saved under ...\binance-review\docs\;
  - 5 WebFetch page reads (4 Binance announcements, 1 The Block article).
- Scripts are my own, in C:\Users\kadir\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-kadir-OneDrive-Masa-st--Wawe-Journal-astro\97ee93d7-3b56-4094-909f-8a419fcb57d4\scratchpad\agents3\binance-review-scripts\. The researcher's three files were re-checked read-only against fresh HEAD ETags.
- No repository change, no production, Supabase or Storage access.

Confirmed:
- URL and listing scheme: 220 objects, not truncated; CRC64NVME appears exactly from the 2025-02 object; the naive regex finds 180 of 220; path-style URLs only; no multipart ETags; ETag equals MD5 on 4 files.
- Publication-lag figures: the BTC numbers match, and the first-Monday pattern holds since 2025-05. The research said since 2025-06.
- CHECKSUM format and the sha256 check.
- ZIP layout on all 4 files, including the 2025 monthly.
- The verbatim zlib-only extractor:
  - its output is byte-identical to Python zipfile;
  - it handles a bit-3 data-descriptor variant;
  - it rejects all 17 corruption cases, as expected;
  - the research's 20/20 test suite reproduces.
- CSV columns: no header, 12 columns, ignore column always '0', at most 2 significant decimals.
- Microseconds from 2025: proven on the 2025-01 monthly. All 44,640 rows are 16-digit and the file starts at 1735689600000000. README.md:11, commit de6bdec, issue #386 and spot CHANGELOG 2024-12-17 (opt-in µs on the REST API) all agree, and the research's parser ingests the whole µs month cleanly.
- Quality: the ETH 2020-06-28 02:00-05:29Z gap (210 min) is reproduced, and the official notice says trading resumed at 05:30 UTC. The 2023-03-24 size anomaly is reproduced.
- Volume: the BTC subtotal (175,914,155 B) and every derived total are exact. A full BTC month gzips to 0.62 MB, inside the projection.
- Terms: every quote and line number is verbatim. The terms are v1.0, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; §3.4, §4.1, §4.3 and §4.4 support the blocker. The PDF matches the markdown. The precedents check out: #478 got only a pointer to the terms and was closed on 2026-10-13; #482 got the same pointer; #514 and #511 have no reply. Monetization is confirmed in PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md:39/211/267/302.

Refuted or corrected:
1. "No CORS, so browser-direct is impossible" is false. The regional S3 path-style endpoint returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on GET from any origin; the research's HEAD test could not detect this. The legal conclusion still stands.
2. The 2021-09-29 announcement URL is broken.
3. The 2020-06-28 start time is not in the cited notice.
4. The memory (6.3 MB) and JSON size (40-48 B/candle) bounds are slightly low: a 31-day BTC month is 7.06 MB of CSV and 49.4 B/candle.

Issues to fold into the plan, all low except CORS (medium):
- Make the current-month update merge the new day into the existing partial object; otherwise the '4 GETs a day' figure is wrong.
- Make the checksum regex tolerant of the ' *' separator.
- Rely on 404-retry rather than a 03:00 UTC schedule; 2024 daily lags reached about 5.6 h.
- Align 1w candles to Monday.
- Reword issue #400 as unconfirmed and likely futures.
- Add an absolute inflate cap.
- Note the 2026-10-16 syntax-only revision of the terms.

Not verified because of the cap: the ETH subtotal, list-type=2, daily-prefix pagination (the arithmetic is consistent), and whether halts hit every symbol at once.

Verdict: sound with fixes. The BLOCKER recommendation, an owner/legal decision before any Binance import, is well supported.
